$comment: M1.7 / T-GW-04 — THE FROZEN WIRE SHAPE OF A DISCOVERED BUSINESS RULE.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AT ALL. The rule-reuse loop crosses two services:
qe-explorer  app/rules.DiscoveredRule.as_dict()     (produces, on completion)
-> POST /internal/crawls/{id}/complete  coverage.discovered_rules
qe-central   app/services/rule_store._clean()       (consumes, persists)
qe-central   app/services/rule_store.fetch_rules()  (produces, on dispatch)
-> POST /crawl  known_rules
qe-explorer  app/rules.DiscoveredRule.from_mapping() (consumes, reuses)
Neither service can test the other. Both ship a top-level `app` package, so a
single pytest process cannot import both — which is precisely why this seam
was proven only in halves. A rename of `field_label` on either side passed
both suites and silently turned every reused rule back into a repeated
experiment: the T-GW-04 acceptance would report success while the learning
loop was severed. A dropped loop is SILENT by construction, because falling
back to re-running the experiment still produces a correct crawl.
So the contract is frozen HERE, as data, and each side asserts against it in
its own process. A rename on either side now fails that side's own suite.
The file is the shared vocabulary; the two tests are the two halves of one
proof that could not otherwise be written.
CHANGING THIS FILE IS A PROTOCOL CHANGE. Bump schema_version, ship the
reader on both sides FIRST (both parsers are fail-closed on an unknown
version, so an unrecognised rule is ignored rather than misapplied), and add
the new version here beside this one rather than editing it in place.
